bytes.scope: INT64 MAX operands are not AllReduce physical wire bytes. An alternative exchanges each word as two INT32 lanes with AllGather and merges locally. Sparse processor-control packets and fallback rows are separate.

constraints: Keep all target projection MACs and BF16 rounding. The dense reader can read the all-gathered TP-major logits, map sampled rows in place and cast as it scans. It keeps IndexCheck, state/seed, final ID casts, rejection kernel and original ArgMax durations as a replacement cost. Conditional on no full-score reader and legal original row/mutation semantics. The full dense traffic of the collective is unchanged in this variant.

For summary, after per-vocab-shard decisions, gather 1–2 INT64 words per sampled row as INT32 lanes and merge locally. Baseline credits only original gather time after latest participant entry, with archive offset bounds. The replacement proxies use the two prior concurrent TP8 12-float medians, retaining old full ArgMax time as local/global selection budget. Packet sizes and operator/launch contexts differ. One phase assumes a common control plan; dependent bonus/target state may require two sequential exchanges. If any dense reader survives keep its exact data. Restore tied IDs/padding, signed zero, ordered masks/boosts and coordinated exceptional-row fallback.

Dense score reuse in DSpark: retain its original base projection, TP8 gather and transpose. At each of five dependent W2 outputs preserve the first BF16 projection rounding, the per-token base row and the separately rounded BF16 sum before ArgMax, then the original cast/ID write. Fuse existing slice, Add and select so the score-bank writeback is avoidable only without a raw score reader. Retain all five W2 and embedding gathers, all ArgMax cost and half (or all) of Add time. Direct strided reads, tile reductions and extra spills can lower or reverse savings. B1 has no wide score copy or slice in this archive.

Traffic-only extra epilogue estimates vs a separate already optimized reader: price one BF16 result write/read per W2 or target GEMM at twice the median one-payload copy rate, before any local-reduction or store-layout overhead. These overlap other scenarios. All-typed-free removes the named score operations and target collective with zero replacement, retaining required GEMMs and all other work. The wider bracket-free case additionally credits every post-head gap and all service until last selection on each branch but retains the five W2 durations. The independent-rank relaxation additionally lets target and draft each select their longest scheduled rank bracket per wave, propagating their sum to all ranks and every inclusive client deadline.

All 16 ranks and every target/draft vocab call in the pinned eager stream are bound to nonoverlapping target intervals; 227 graph and four eager anchors per rank. Validate read head B/M against actual worker request membership and rows. Discard unscheduled graphs and give dummy DPs no credit. Each included wave advances the latest next-target entry under saved cross-rank clock bounds and freezes other work. A client gets credit for inclusive waves started by its original first chunk/end on at least one scheduled DP, then recompute the eight-request maximum. This is a favorable publication/serial propagation assumption; asynchronous queues or earlier publication can hide time. No physical speedup ceiling or new output validation.

Ordinary estimates use the actual number of verification steps, one target/one draft sequence per DP, one-row prompt and six-row verification costs from frozen C8 with one active request on that DP. When that prompt shape is absent on the requested DP borrow the other DP. Realized shared-resource exposure and natural load mixture are not measured. The historical 1104 metadata observations cover a separate run; missing badword/holder information is not proof that a fast branch is legal.

Raw/full logits, entropy, random/penalty processors and external/custom readers require separate sufficient outputs or dense fallback. Top-k/selected logprobs also require logsumexp, score of each requested token and tie-correct global rank; an argmax pair alone cannot satisfy them. Keep per-row original RNG and processor state order in stochastic/heterogeneous batches.
